title: SAO Nunchuck - SAO++ edition
credit: Original design: Andy and Jared Geppert (ageppert), SAO Nunchuck V1.0, 2024, MIT license, github.com/ageppert/SAO_Nunchuck
notes: A passive adaptor: the badge's 3.3 V, ground and I2C lines go straight to a Nunchuck plug. No chip, no LED, no resistor.
BADGE POWER ONLY. No coin cell and no SAO / OFF / BAT switch (a recorded exception to docs/standard.md section 3): there is nothing
to light, and a Nunchuck is only useful while the badge is talking to it. With no cell on the board nothing can back-feed one.
No I2C pull-ups on the board (docs/standard.md section 1; the maker fitted none either). A Nunchuck answers at I2C address 0x52.
J1 is the only part that is bought and placed.
X2 is board copper: five gold fingers on the board edge (three on the back, two on the front) that the Nunchuck plug grips.
X3 and X4 are the maker's two Qwiic sockets (JST SH 4-pin, SM04B-SRSS-TB): pads only, NOT FITTED, not in the BOM.
Solder one on by hand to chain other 3.3 V I2C boards. SAO GPIO1 and GPIO2 are not used.
